name: MARE
full_name: Microcalorimeter Arrays for a Rhenium Experiment
summary: MARE was a coordinated research programme to scale calorimetric neutrino-mass measurements beyond MANU and MiBeta. It investigated rhenium absorbers and large cryogenic arrays, but was discontinued in 2013 after detector-performance difficulties; later efforts concentrated on holmium-163.
detection_principle: The radioactive isotope is contained inside a low-temperature absorber. Arrays measure beta-decay energy calorimetrically, seeking the small endpoint distortion due to the undetected neutrino mass.

status.label: Programme discontinued / historical
status.evidence: The participating Bicocca detector laboratory states that MARE was abandoned in 2013 after rhenium-based microcalorimeters failed to meet the reproducible performance required for a sub-eV neutrino-mass experiment. The intended final sensitivity was never achieved.

timeline.event: The MARE programme was discontinued following detector-performance difficulties; subsequent work concentrated on holmium-163 calorimetry.

results.summary: The collaboration described a staged development programme; its final sub-eV configuration was not an achieved measurement.

science_scope: This is a laboratory kinematic measurement of the effective electron-flavour neutrino mass. Its observable differs from the effective Majorana mass in neutrinoless double-beta decay and the sum of neutrino masses inferred from cosmology.
